The `miniast` package round-trips a raw parse tree into typed nodes and back into source: `raw parse tree --(Rebuilder)--> miniast nodes --(AsStringVisitor)--> source`. It currently supports the plain `try/except` statement (the `Try` node) but NOT Python's `try/except*` exception-group statement. A parser already emits raw nodes of kind `"TryStar"` (each raw TryStar has a `"body"` list of statements and a `"handlers"` list of raw `ExceptHandler` nodes, exactly like raw `Try`), but `miniast.roundtrip()` currently raises on them because the new node type is not registered.

Add full support for the `TryStar` node so a raw `try/except*` round-trips to source. A node type is only "supported" in `miniast` when it is registered in ALL THREE of the library's parallel dispatch tables, and they must agree on exactly the same set of node types:

1. `miniast/nodes.py`: define a new `TryStar(Node)` class with the SAME `_fields` as `Try` (`("body", "handlers")`), and add it to the `ALL_NODE_CLASSES` registry tuple so `is_supported(TryStar)` is true.

2. `miniast/rebuilder.py`: add `Rebuilder.visit_TryStar(self, raw)` that rebuilds a raw TryStar (kind `"TryStar"`) into a `nodes.TryStar`, recursively rebuilding its `body` statements and its `handlers` (reuse the same handler/body rebuilding the `Try` path uses). After this, `Rebuilder().visit(raw)` must not raise `UnsupportedNodeError` for a TryStar.

3. `miniast/as_string.py`: add `AsStringVisitor.visit_TryStar(self, node)` that renders the node back to source. It must render the header as `try:` followed by the indented body, then each handler rendered with `except*` (a star after `except`) instead of plain `except` -- i.e. handlers under a `TryStar` print `except* E as n:` / `except*:` rather than `except E as n:`. Do NOT change how plain `Try`/`ExceptHandler` render under a normal `try`.

The three tables must stay in lockstep: if `TryStar` is registered in only some of them, rebuilding or rendering a `try/except*` still fails. Keep `miniast/raw.py` and `miniast/version.py` exactly as they are -- `raw.py` mentions `"TryStar"` only as a label in its raw-kind catalog and is not one of the dispatch tables. Existing `Try`/`Pass`/`Assign` behavior must continue to round-trip unchanged.
